# basenc, dircolors, hostid, mkfifo, mknod, numfmt, pathchk, pinky, pr,
# ptx, shred, stdbuf, stty and sync. Nothing here depends on the clock, a
# terminal, the CPU (numfmt keeps below 19 digits, where x86-64 and arm64
# GNU agree) or randomness (shred's patterns beyond three passes).

basenc --base64 a.txt
basenc --base64url words
basenc --base32hex a.txt
basenc --base16 a.txt
basenc --base16 -d < a.txt; echo $?
env echo 68656c6c6f | basenc --base16 -d
basenc --base2msbf -w 20 b.txt
basenc --base2lsbf b.txt | basenc --base2lsbf -d
env printf hell | basenc --z85
env printf hello | basenc --z85
env printf 'xK#0@' | basenc --z85 -d
basenc a.txt
basenc --base64 --base16 a.txt
basenc --base16 --base64 a.txt

dircolors -p | head -20
SHELL=/bin/bash TERM=xterm dircolors
SHELL=/bin/tcsh TERM=xterm-256color dircolors
TERM=dumb dircolors -b
COLORTERM=truecolor TERM=dumb dircolors -c
TERM=xterm dircolors --print-ls-colors | head -5
env -u SHELL dircolors
dircolors -b -p
dircolors -p x
dircolors a b
env printf 'TERM *\nDIR 01;34\nBOGUS 1\nLINK\n' > db; dircolors -b db
env printf '.TAR 01;31\n*it:s= 1\n' | dircolors -b -

hostid
hostid x

mkfifo p; ls -l p | cut -c1-10
mkfifo -m 600 p; stat -c %a p
mkfifo -m u=rw,go=r p; stat -c %a p
mkfifo -m 1666 p
mkfifo -m bad p
mkfifo a.txt
mkfifo
mkfifo nodir/p q; stat -c %F q
mknod p p; stat -c %F p
mknod p
mknod p c
mknod p c 1
mknod p p 1 2
mknod p z 1 2
mknod p c x 2
mknod -m 600 q pipe; stat -c '%a %F' q

numfmt --to=si 1000 1500000 9999 999999 1 0 -- -1500
numfmt --to=iec 1024 2047 --to=iec-i 1048576
numfmt --from=si 1K 1k 0.5K --from=auto 1Ki
numfmt --from=iec-i 1K
numfmt 1K
numfmt --invalid=warn abc 5 --invalid=fail x
numfmt --round=down --to=si 1999
numfmt --round=nearest --to=si 1450 -- -1450
numfmt --format=%010f 1234 --format='pre %.2f post' 3.14159
numfmt --format=%d 5
numfmt --padding=-8 42; numfmt --padding=0 5
numfmt --suffix=B --to=iec 1024 --from-unit=512
numfmt --header --field=2 --to=si < words
env printf '  1000 2000\n 300 4\n' | numfmt --to=si
env printf 'a:1000:b\n' | numfmt -d: --field=2 --to=si
env printf '1000 2000\n3000 x\n4000\n' | numfmt --to=si --field=1-2
numfmt --debug 5
numfmt --to=auto 5
numfmt --field=0 5

pathchk a.txt dir/new; echo $?
pathchk -p 'a b/c' abcdefghijklmnop ok
pathchk -P x/-y ''
pathchk --portability -a
pathchk a.txt/x
pathchk
pathchk ''

pinky
pinky -fq
pinky -l root
pinky -l nosuchuser
pinky -l

pr -t a.txt
pr -3 -t words
pr -2 -a -t a.txt b.txt
pr -m -t a.txt b.txt
pr -m -t -s, a.txt csv
pr -n -t a.txt
pr -n:3 -N 9 -t words
pr -d -o 2 -t b.txt
pr -l 15 a.txt
pr -l 12 -h Title -f words
pr -D %F -l 11 b.txt
pr +2 -l 11 words
pr --pages=1:1 -l 11 words
pr -c -t tabs
pr -e4 -t tabs
pr -W 10 -t words
pr -J -2 -t words
pr -T a.txt b.txt
pr -l x a.txt
pr -2 -m a.txt b.txt
pr nope a.txt
pr -r nope a.txt

ptx words
ptx -w 40 words
ptx -A a.txt b.txt
ptx -r words
ptx -O words
ptx -T -M entry words
ptx -G words
ptx -f -g 5 csv
ptx -W '[a-z]+' -S '\n' words
env printf 'the\n' > stop; ptx -i stop words
env printf 'fox\n' > only; ptx -o only words
ptx -F '...' -w 30 words
ptx -g 0 words
ptx -W '\(' words

shred -n 0 -z -s 0 -v a.txt; cat a.txt
shred -n 0 -z -x a.txt; od -c a.txt
shred -v --remove=wipe -n0 a.txt; ls
shred -u -v -n0 words; ls
shred nope
shred -n x a.txt
shred --remove=bad a.txt
shred
mkdir d; shred d

stdbuf -oL echo hi
stdbuf -iL true
stdbuf true
stdbuf -o x true
stdbuf -oL
stdbuf -e0 nosuchcommand

stty
stty -a -g
stty -a echo
stty bogus
stty intr
stty -echo -bogus
stty -F nope
stty min x

sync a.txt; echo $?
sync nope
sync -d
sync -d -f a.txt
sync -f a.txt b.txt; echo $?
